name: pokec
title: Pokec: who is influential, and where
description: Pokec social network: each row is a directed friendship from the first user to the second.

steps.ask: Who are the 10 most influential users?
steps.say: A first question. The plan, the reading of the file (directed, 30.6 million friendships) and the measure chosen for "influential" are on screen before the answer is trusted.

steps.ask: Which region is each of them from?
steps.say: A drill-down. The ranking is not computed again: the steps marked reused carry the same lineage key as in turn 1.
A changed parameter. Only the last step runs; the scores are reused, and the longer list is cut from the full scores, not from the earlier list of 10.
Meanwhile the edge file grows: new rows arrive, as they would from a nightly load. Nobody tells the system.

steps.ask: Who are the 10 most influential users?
steps.say: The same words as turn 1. The plan is replayed without a model call, but nothing computed on the old file is reused: the change was noticed from the file itself, and the answer is different.

steps.ask: Who are the 10 most influential users within region "{x}"?
steps.say: The safety moment. This request has two readings that give different answers. Both contracts are shown with what each would reuse, and nothing runs until one is chosen. The recorded user picks B, then looks at A to see how far the two differ.

steps.ask: Among the 20 most influential users, what is the largest group in which every two are friends, ignoring the direction of friendships, and who is in it?
steps.say: A request no operator computes. The system says so, prepares the 20-user subgraph with checked steps, and has two functions written separately; the value is shown only because both agree, and it is marked as an answer by code.

close: The session details hold the session's bill: steps reused against executed, computation not repeated, model calls and fees, turns replayed. The audit record holds every plan, every reuse decision with its key, and every check.
